description: Coverage matrix for the advertised haskell.nix baseline. Comparison rows have real targets on both sides. Failing rows are required haskell.nix parity capabilities that penance does not implement yet.

phases.title: Cabal project translation
phases.notes: Tracks haskell.nix cabalProject' / plan-nix baseline against the current penance committed-lock path.

phases.title: Cabal component derivations
phases.notes: Tracks the advertised component-derivation baseline for an executable component.

phases.title: Backpack project build
phases.notes: Tracks Backpack build parity on the local multi-instantiation fixture.

phases.title: Stack project translation
phases.failure: haskell.nix advertises Stack project translation through project' / stackProject'; penance intentionally has no Stack parser or benchmark fixture yet.
phases.notes: Add a Stack fixture and a penance lock path or mark Stack unsupported by explicit product decision.

phases.title: Hackage package-set builds
phases.failure: haskell.nix ships hackage.nix-backed package sets; penance only has surface validation smoke tests and no lock-backed Hackage unit builder benchmark.
phases.notes: Turn this into a comparison when penance can lock and build a selected Hackage package and dependency closure.

phases.title: Stackage snapshot package-set builds
phases.failure: haskell.nix ships stackage.nix snapshots; penance has a Stackage closure benchmark but no STRATA snapshot lock or build path.
phases.notes: Turn this into a comparison when snapshot.yaml generation and lock-backed Stackage builds exist.

phases.title: shellFor development environment
phases.failure: haskell.nix exposes shellFor, ghcWithPackages, and ghcWithHoogle; penance does not yet expose a lock-backed dev shell or HLS projection.
phases.notes: Turn this into a comparison when devShells.<system>.default is backed by external package DB composition.

phases.title: Haskell project cross compilation
phases.failure: haskell.nix exposes projectCross for Haskell projects; penance currently benchmarks only a C-level aarch64 ELF probe, not a full cross Haskell project.
phases.notes: Turn this into a comparison when the aarch64-linux Haskell fixture builds through the target toolchain lane.

phases.title: Project variants, modules, and overrides
phases.failure: haskell.nix exposes projectVariants, appendModule, extend, overlays, modules, and extras; penance does not yet have an equivalent override/materialization benchmark.
phases.notes: Turn this into a comparison when STRATA lock overrides and kill-switch variants are benchmarked.

phases.title: Tests, benchmarks, and checks collection
phases.failure: haskell.nix exposes test, benchmark, and check collection helpers; penance has no benchmark fixture proving these component classes end to end.
phases.notes: Turn this into a comparison when the fixture contains tests and benchmarks and penance exposes matching build/check attrs.

phases.title: Plan materialization and cache workflow
phases.failure: haskell.nix supports materialized plan outputs and cache-oriented workflows; penance still lacks the CA realisation / cache-anchor parity benchmark.
phases.notes: Turn this into a comparison when M3 cache realisation or anchor fallback is implemented and measured.
